title: Burnside's Lemma from Orbit-Stabilizer
description: Derives Burnside's counting lemma from the orbit-stabilizer theorem via a double counting argument. Proves the Fubini-type identity for finite group actions.

meta.author: Burnside (1897), Cauchy (1845), Frobenius (1887)
meta.assumptions: No axioms. All results proved from Mathlib. Original contribution: double counting identity via sum_boole + sum_comm.
originalContributions: Double counting identity: Σ_g |Fix(g)| = Σ_x |Stab(x)| via sum_boole + sum_comm
Explicit derivation chain from Lagrange to Burnside

overview.historicalContext: Burnside's lemma (also called the Cauchy-Frobenius lemma) was known to Cauchy (1845) and Frobenius (1887) before Burnside popularized it in his 1897 textbook. It is one of the most useful counting tools in combinatorics, reducing orbit-counting problems to fixed-point calculations.
overview.problemStatement: Derive Burnside's counting lemma from the orbit-stabilizer theorem.
overview.text: The derivation chain: Lagrange → Orbit-Stabilizer → Double Counting → Burnside.
overview.proofStrategy: Three-step derivation: (1) orbit-stabilizer from Lagrange via coset bijection, (2) double counting via Fubini for finite sums, (3) Burnside from orbit-stabilizer + double counting.
keyInsights: The double counting identity (Σ_g |Fix(g)| = Σ_x |Stab(x)|) is proved by expressing both sides as indicator sums and swapping via Finset.sum_comm.
Orbit-stabilizer follows from Lagrange's theorem via the bijection Orb(x) ≃ G/Stab(x).
Burnside's lemma is the final step: each orbit contributes |G|/|O| × |O| = |G| to the stabilizer sum, giving total = |X/G| × |G|.

conclusion.summary: Burnside's counting lemma is a direct consequence of the orbit-stabilizer theorem (itself from Lagrange) combined with a double counting argument.
conclusion.implications: This derivation chain shows that the core of Burnside's lemma is Lagrange's theorem. The double counting step is a Fubini-type identity for finite sums.
